note: The Log Book, for agents (17 October 2026). Every name and number on screen is made up.

scenes.headline: The Log Book, for agents
scenes.sub: Log it, hand it in, watch it go
scenes.line: This is the new Log Book, as an agent sees it. Log your documents, hand them in, and watch them go.

scenes.headline: Your number, your password
scenes.line: Open Ricky Rampersad branch dot com, slash log book. Sign in with your agent number, and the password you use for the fact find.

scenes.headline: It knows where it goes
scenes.line: Choose the document first. The Log Book routes it to the right department, from the branch's own history, and says how sure it is.

scenes.headline: Only your clients
scenes.line: Then find the client. Type a name, an e-mail, or a policy number. You only ever see your own clients. Tick the policy the papers are for.

scenes.headline: What usually comes with it
scenes.line: If something usually travels with it, the Log Book asks. A surrender usually comes with proof of I D. One tap adds it.

scenes.headline: A reference, at once
scenes.line: Confirm the papers are complete and signed, and press Log it. You get a reference. Hand the papers to the branch the same day.

scenes.headline: Every step, on your phone
scenes.line: My log shows every step. Logged. Received by the branch. Sent on a transmittal. And confirmed by the department.

scenes.headline: The same day

rows.b: In by four, out the same day
rows.i: Stamped when you log, when the branch receives, when it goes

rows.b: Late? The branch is asked why
rows.i: And you are copied on the e-mail

rows.b: A contract to deliver: twenty days
rows.i: Chased at day fifteen and day eighteen

scenes.line: The aim is the same day. Papers in by four o'clock go out the same day. If not, the branch is asked why, and you are copied. A contract you collect to deliver has twenty days.

scenes.headline: Your whole team
scenes.line: Unit managers see their whole team, under My team. Every agent's papers, or one agent at a time. Nobody sees another unit.
Log it. Hand it in. Watch it go.
